newsitem.title: UK: RALLYING-SCHWARZ UNDERLINES RAC RALLY SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SCHWARZ UNDERLINES RAC RALLY SUPREMACY.

text.p: German Armin Schwarz dominated the second leg of the three-day RAC Rally on Sunday as his rivals fell by the wayside in a series of spectacular accidents in treacherous conditions.

Schawarz, driving for the Toyota team as they made their return to top-class rallying after a year's ban for cheating, finished the day more than five minutes clear of his nearest challenger Masao Kamioka of Japan in a Subaru.
After two days of driving in snow and ice, Schwarz was fastest in nine of the 17 special stages contested through forests and the asphalt roads of stately homes and race circuits

"It has been really difficult," said Schwarz. "I tried to concentrate and watch out for the ice. But it has been made much harder because we had to complete the day on just one set of tyres on stages which changed from ice to soft snow to wet tarmac."
Behind Kamioka, who said he owed his success to growing up in northern Japan where he became used to snow and ice, was Swedish veteran Stig Blomqvist, 50, winner in 1971, in a Skoda kit car.
Fancied Britons Robbie Head, in a Renault, and Gwyndaf Evans, in a Ford, crashed on the second stage at Chatsworth. Head's car barrel-rolled five times and Evans' twice.
Somehow Evans managed to complete the stage before being taken to hospital where he was detained with severe whiplash injuries to his back, neck and head.
Formula One driver Martin Brundle of Britain was languished in 73rd position, more than one hour and 43 minutes behind Schwarz at the end of the day.
